```{r Preliminaries, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, warning=F}
#Turn off the informational messages in dplyr when using the summarise() function.
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
#
#On Windows the default temporary path can be long enough to break workbook creation, so R is pointed
#at a shorter temporary directory through .Renviron, which takes effect in later sessions. This runs on
#Windows only: elsewhere Sys.getenv("R_USER") is empty, and the previous version of this line wrote to
#the filesystem root and left R writing its scratch files into a directory named after the unevaluated
#call. An existing .Renviron is added to rather than overwritten.
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows" && nzchar(Sys.getenv("R_USER"))) {
  short_tmp <- file.path(Sys.getenv("R_USER"), "Rtmp")
  dir.create(short_tmp, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  renviron_file <- file.path(Sys.getenv("R_USER"), ".Renviron")
  renviron_lines <- if (file.exists(renviron_file)) readLines(renviron_file, warn = FALSE) else character(0)
  if (!any(grepl("^TMPDIR=", renviron_lines))) {
    writeLines(c(renviron_lines, paste0("TMPDIR=", short_tmp)), renviron_file)
  }
}
#
#MCMCglmmProc rounds pMCMC values for fixed effects to three decimal places
#and comparisons between fixed effects to five. Because round() drops trailing
#zeros, tables can mix values such as 0.1, 0.28 and 0.02071.
#This function displays estimates and intervals to two decimal places and
#pMCMC values to three, except values below 0.001, which are shown as "< 0.001".
#This includes values previously rounded to zero; it does not recover precision
#lost through earlier rounding. Header rows and other text are left untouched.
format_table = function(tab) {
  interval <- "^-?[0-9.]+ \\(-?[0-9.]+, ?-?[0-9.]+\\)$"

  tidy_interval <- function(x) vapply(x, function(v) {
    n <- as.numeric(regmatches(v, gregexpr("-?[0-9.]+", v))[[1]])
    sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", n[1], n[2], n[3])
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

  # Format posterior modes and their intervals.
  est <- grepl(interval, tab[[2]])
  tab[[2]][est] <- tidy_interval(tab[[2]][est])

  # The third column contains pMCMC for fixed effects and I2 intervals
  # for random effects. Format numeric entries without changing text labels.
  pv <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(tab[[3]]))
  numeric_rows <- which(!is.na(pv))

  tab[[3]][numeric_rows] <- ifelse(
    pv[numeric_rows] < 0.001,
    "< 0.001",
    sprintf("%.3f", pv[numeric_rows]))

  # Format I2 estimates and their intervals to two decimal places.
  i2 <- grepl(interval, tab[[3]])
  tab[[3]][i2] <- tidy_interval(tab[[3]][i2])

  tab
}
#
#Every Extended Data table has the same shape: a term in the first column, then
#one or two pairs of estimate and pMCMC columns, with section rows separating
#fixed from random effects. flextable is used rather than kableExtra because it
#renders to Word, HTML and PDF from the same code, whereas kableExtra's HTML
#styling is dropped when the document is knitted to Word.
si_table <- function(tab, caption, panel_labels = NULL,
                     sections = NULL, footnote = NULL) {
  if (is.null(sections)) {
    sections <- grep("^Fixed|^Random", tab[[1]])
  }
  #Preserve displayed labels while making internal column names unique.
  shown <- names(tab)
  names(tab) <- make.unique(names(tab))
  ft <- flextable(tab)
  # Body-row indices shift only when the column labels are moved into it.
  body_offset <- 0L
  if (!is.null(panel_labels)) {
    #Only the universal panel labels remain in the repeating header.
    ft <- delete_part(ft, part = "header")
    ft <- add_header_row(
      ft,
      values = panel_labels,
      colwidths = c(1, 2, 2))
    ft <- align(
      ft,
      i = 1,
      align = "center",
      part = "header")
    #Display the column labels once, as the first body row.
    ft <- add_body_row(
      ft,
      values = shown,
      colwidths = rep(1L, ncol(tab)),
      top = TRUE)
    body_offset <- 1L
    ft <- bold(ft, i = 1, part = "body")
    ft <- bg(ft, i = 1, bg = "#E7E5E5", part = "body")
  } else {
    ft <- set_header_labels(
      ft,
      values = setNames(as.list(shown), names(tab)))
  }

  #Caption: bold table label, followed by the explanatory text.
  lab <- regmatches(
    caption,
    regexpr("^[^.]*\\.\\s*", caption))
  body <- substring(caption, nchar(lab) + 1)
  cap_props <- fp_text_default(font.family = "Times New Roman")
  ft <- set_caption(ft,
                    caption = as_paragraph(as_chunk(lab,
                                                    props = update(cap_props, bold = TRUE)),
                                           as_chunk(body, props = cap_props)))
  #Repeating header.
  ft <- bold(ft, part = "header")
  ft <- bg(ft, bg = "#E7E5E5", part = "header")
  if (!is.null(panel_labels)) {
  header_border <- officer::fp_border(color = "black", width = 0.75)
  #Above and below the repeating panel-label row.
  ft <- hline_top(ft, border = header_border, part = "header")
  ft <- hline_bottom(ft, border = header_border, part = "header")
  #Below the non-repeating column-label row.
  ft <- hline(ft, i = 1, border = header_border, part = "body")
}
  #Section rows, adjusted for the inserted body row.
  if (length(sections)) {
    ft <- bold(ft, 
               i = sections + body_offset,
               part = "body")
    ft <- bg(ft,
             i = sections + body_offset,
             bg = "#E7E5E5",
             part = "body")
  }
  ft <- align(ft, j = 1, align = "left", part = "all")
  ft <- align(ft,
              j = seq(2, ncol(tab)),
              align = "center",
              part = "all")

  #Significant pMCMC and p values, adjusted for the inserted body row.
  for (j in grep("^pMCMC|: p$", shown)) {
    p_text <- trimws(as.character(tab[[j]]))
    p_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(p_text))
    sig <- which(p_text == "< 0.001" |
                   (!is.na(p_num) & p_num < 0.05))
    if (length(sig)) {
      ft <- bold(ft,
                 i = sig + body_offset,
                 j = j,
                 part = "body")
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(footnote)) {
    ft <- add_footer_lines(ft, footnote)
  }
  ft <- fontsize(ft, size = 8, part = "all")
  ft <- font(ft, fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all")
  ft <- padding(ft, padding = 2, part = "all")
  set_table_properties(
    autofit(ft),
    layout = "autofit",
    width = 1,
    align = "left",
    opts_word = list(repeat_headers = TRUE))
}
#
#
#function to combine main effects and two-way interactions from different MCMCglmm models
model_combine = function(M,I2){
combM<-I2#Highest order model
combM$Sol[1:dim(M$Sol)[1],1:dim(M$Sol)[2]]<-M$Sol#Replace main effect in model object
return(combM)
}
#
#MCMCglmmProc applies fixed_names by position, so if a model's fixed effects ever come back in a
#different order the names are silently attached to the wrong terms. The order of factor levels, and
#therefore of the fixed effects, can change with the collation locale. This check stops the document
#rather than letting a mislabelled table through.
check_fixed_order = function(model, expected) {
  if (!identical(colnames(model$Sol), expected)) {
    stop("Fixed effects are not in the order the table names assume.\n  found:    ",
         paste(colnames(model$Sol), collapse = ", "),
         "\n  expected: ", paste(expected, collapse = ", "))
  }
}
#The order Extended Data Table 5 and st_eggs_excl_1coop name their fixed effects in
BS2_terms = c("BS_2Cheat", "BS_2Coop_w/o_Cheat", "BS_2Coop_w_Cheat", "ZnoFOther", "logit_prop.BrokenInc",
              "BS_2Cheat:ZnoFCoops", "BS_2Coop_w/o_Cheat:ZnoFCoops", "BS_2Coop_w_Cheat:ZnoFCoops",
              "BS_2Cheat:ZnoFCoops2", "BS_2Coop_w/o_Cheat:ZnoFCoops2", "BS_2Coop_w_Cheat:ZnoFCoops2")
#
#Distribution variance for the I2 denominator of a Poisson (log link) model. The distribution-specific
#variance on the latent scale is ln(1 + 1/lambda), with lambda the fitted mean on the data scale
#(Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2010; de Villemereuil et al. 2016). It is computed from the same model object
#that is passed to MCMCglmmProc so that the variance components and lambda come from one model.
poisson_dist_var = function(model) log(1 + 1 / mean(predict(model)))
#
#function to combine main effects, two-way interactions and three-way interactions from different MCMCglmm models
model_combine2 = function(M,I2,I3){
combM<-I3#Highest order model
combM$Sol[1:dim(M$Sol)[1],1:dim(M$Sol)[2]]<-M$Sol#Replace main effect in model object
combM$Sol[1:dim(I2$Sol)[1],(1+dim(M$Sol)[2]):dim(I2$Sol)[2]]<-I2$Sol[1:dim(I2$Sol)[1],(1+dim(M$Sol)[2]):dim(I2$Sol)[2]]#Replace two-way interactions effect in model object
return(combM)
}
#
```

```{r Table processing, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
#R markdown table
st_eggs<-xl_2_df(xltab=Cheating_SItablesXL,sheet="Suppl. Table 5 all groups")
st_eggs <- format_table(st_eggs)
#
#**Extended Data Table 5: differences between the fitted curves for cooperators with and without cheats*
#The quadratic contrast above shows that the two curves differ in shape, but not at which group sizes
#they differ. These rows test that directly: at each number of cooperators the fitted value for
#cooperators in groups with cheats is subtracted from the fitted value for cooperators in groups
#without cheats, for every posterior sample.
#Note these are computed from m_eggs_quad_c1 rather than from the st_activity_display object st_eggs_model, because st_eggs_model takes the
#intercepts from the main-effects-only model m_eggs_main_c1 and the fitted curves require all terms to come
#from the same model.
#Number of cooperators was z-transformed before modelling, so the plotted values 1 to 5 are first
#converted to the z-scale using the mean and sd of the model data, and squared to give the quadratic term
zCoops_S4 <- (1:5 - mean(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)) / sd(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)
#The other covariates are held at their overall mean, the same value for both strategies, so that the
#comparison isolates breeding strategy. Under the log link of the Poisson model the covariate terms do
#not cancel as they would on an identity scale, so a common value has to be chosen rather than each
#strategy's own mean
zOther_S4  <- mean(df_eggs$ZnoFOther)
broken_S4  <- mean(df_eggs$logit_prop.BrokenInc)
#The log link is non-linear, so fitted counts are averaged over the random-effect distribution, taken
#at the midpoints of 40 equal-probability slices of a normal. The year variance is left out of that
#average and the fitted values are divided by the overall fitted value: dividing a count by its annual
#mean removes the year effect, so this expresses the differences as reproductive investment relative
#to the annual mean, the same scale as Fig. 2A
REnodes_S4 <- qnorm(seq(0.5/40, 1 - 0.5/40, length.out = 40))
V_S4 <- rowSums(m_eggs_quad_c1$VCV[, colnames(m_eggs_quad_c1$VCV) != "year"])
fitted_S4 <- function(strategy, z){
  eta <- m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy)] +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, "ZnoFOther"] * zOther_S4 +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, "logit_prop.BrokenInc"] * broken_S4 +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy, ":ZnoFCoops")]  * z +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy, ":ZnoFCoops2")] * z^2
  rowMeans(sapply(REnodes_S4, function(u) exp(eta + sqrt(V_S4) * u)))
}
#Reference value: the fitted value averaged over the composition of the observed data
zAll_S4 <- (df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp - mean(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)) / sd(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)
ref_S4  <- rowMeans(sapply(seq_len(nrow(df_eggs)), function(i)
  fitted_S4(as.character(df_eggs$BS_2[i]), zAll_S4[i])))
#The three pairs of strategies compared, in the same order as the panels of Fig. 2B, with the names
#they are given in the table
Pairs_S4 <- list(c("Coop_w/o_Cheat", "Coop_w_Cheat"),
                 c("Cheat", "Coop_w_Cheat"),
                 c("Cheat", "Coop_w/o_Cheat"))
PairNames_S4 <- c("Cooperators in groups without cheats vs Cooperators in groups with cheats",
                  "Cheats vs Cooperators in groups with cheats",
                  "Cheats vs Cooperators in groups without cheats")
#Each pair is differenced at each number of cooperators and summarised the same way MCMCglmmProc
#summarises fixed effects: posterior mode, 95% HPD interval and a two-tailed pMCMC bounded below by
#1/(number of posterior samples)
Diffs_S4 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(Pairs_S4), function(k){
  pair <- Pairs_S4[[k]]
  draws <- as.mcmc(sapply(zCoops_S4, function(z)
    (fitted_S4(pair[1], z) - fitted_S4(pair[2], z)) / ref_S4))
  pm  <- round(posterior.mode(draws), 2)
  hpd <- round(HPDinterval(draws), 2)
  p   <- round(pmax(0.5 / nrow(draws),
                    pmin(colSums(draws > 0) / nrow(draws),
                         1 - colSums(draws > 0) / nrow(draws))) * 2, 3)
  data.frame('Fixed Effects' = paste0(PairNames_S4[k], " : ", 1:5, " cooperators in group"),
             'Posterior Mode (CI)' = paste0(pm, " (", hpd[,1], ", ", hpd[,2], ")"),
             pMCMC = as.character(p), check.names = FALSE)
}))
#Add the rows to the markdown table, after the existing fixed effect comparisons and before the random
#effects, with a section heading formatted as the other section headings in the table
st_eggs <- rbind(st_eggs[1:(grep("^Random Effects", st_eggs$'Fixed Effects') - 1),],
            data.frame('Fixed Effects' = "Fixed Effect Comparisons: fitted values",
                       'Posterior Mode (CI)' = "Posterior Mode (CI)",
                       pMCMC = "pMCMC", check.names = FALSE),
            Diffs_S4,
            st_eggs[grep("^Random Effects", st_eggs$'Fixed Effects'):nrow(st_eggs),])
rownames(st_eggs) <- NULL
#The rows just added are formatted on the same convention as the rest of the table
st_eggs <- format_table(st_eggs)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.cap = paste0("**Extended Data Figure 2: The number of eggs laid by each breeding strategy in relation to the number of cooperators in the group**. The number of eggs laid by cheats (orange), cooperators in groups without cheats (green) and cooperators in groups with cheats (grey). The number of eggs laid was modelled as a count with year as a random effect, and fitted values are shown relative to the annual mean so that they are comparable with the observed data, which are also expressed relative to the annual mean. Circles and error bars show the mean +/- one standard error, solid lines show fitted values from the Bayesian mixed model (Extended Data Table 5), and shaded ribbons show 95% credible intervals. The differences between these fitted curves are shown in Fig. 2A.", " Sample size: n = ", nrow(df_eggs), " observations from ", length(unique(df_eggs$id)), " females in ", length(unique(df_eggs$yearcamp)), " groups."), fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9, dpi = 600, align = "center"}
#Fitted number of eggs from Model m_eggs_quad_c1 (Poisson, log link), for each breeding strategy across the
#number of cooperators. The log link is non-linear, so fitted counts are averaged over the random-effect
#distribution, taken at the midpoints of 40 equal-probability slices of a normal. The year variance is
#left out of that average and the fitted values are divided by the overall fitted value: dividing a count
#by its annual mean removes the year effect exactly under a log link, so this puts the fit on the same
#"eggs relative to the annual mean" axis as the observed data. Covariates not shown on the axis are held
#at the mean observed within each strategy, so each line matches the groups it summarises.
BSlabels <- c("Cheat" = "Cheats", "Coop_w/o_Cheat" = "Cooperators, no cheat", "Coop_w_Cheat" = "Cooperators, cheat")
coop2_mean <- mean(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)
coop2_sd   <- sd(df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp)
REnodes_eggs <- qnorm(seq(0.5/40, 1 - 0.5/40, length.out = 40))
V_eggs       <- rowSums(m_eggs_quad_c1$VCV[, colnames(m_eggs_quad_c1$VCV) != "year"])
fitted_eggs <- function(strategy, x, zOther, broken){
  z <- (x - coop2_mean) / coop2_sd
  eta <- m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy)] +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy, ":ZnoFCoops")]  * z +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, paste0("BS_2", strategy, ":ZnoFCoops2")] * z^2 +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, "logit_prop.BrokenInc"] * broken +
         m_eggs_quad_c1$Sol[, "ZnoFOther"] * zOther
  rowMeans(sapply(REnodes_eggs, function(u) exp(eta + sqrt(V_eggs) * u)))
}
ref_eggs <- rowMeans(sapply(seq_len(nrow(df_eggs)), function(i)
  fitted_eggs(as.character(df_eggs$BS_2[i]), df_eggs$noFCoopsCamp[i],
             mean(df_eggs$ZnoFOther[df_eggs$BS_2 == df_eggs$BS_2[i]]),
             mean(df_eggs$logit_prop.BrokenInc[df_eggs$BS_2 == df_eggs$BS_2[i]]))))
df_eggs_fit <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Cheat", "Coop_w/o_Cheat", "Coop_w_Cheat"), function(s){
  zOther <- mean(df_eggs$ZnoFOther[df_eggs$BS_2 == s])
  broken <- mean(df_eggs$logit_prop.BrokenInc[df_eggs$BS_2 == s])
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq(1, 5, by = 0.05), function(x){
    pred <- fitted_eggs(s, x, zOther, broken) / ref_eggs
    data.frame(BS_2 = s, noFCoopsCamp = x,
               mean = median(pred), lcl = quantile(pred, 0.025), ucl = quantile(pred, 0.975))
  }))
}))
#Observed means per strategy and group size
df_eggs_all_summary <- df_eggs_all %>%  dplyr::filter(noFCoopsCamp != 0, noFCoopsCamp != 6) %>%
  group_by(noFCoopsCamp, BS_2) %>%

                   lcl = mean(relativeRSInc4, na.rm = TRUE) - (sd(relativeRSInc4)/sqrt(n())),

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Table 14
# Helper functions -----

extract_seg_params <- function(seg_fit, blank_pvals_for = c("U", "G0")) {
  tt <- summary(seg_fit$lme.fit)$tTable
  ci <- t(confint(seg_fit))
  params <- rownames(tt)

  out <- data.frame(
    Parameter = params,
    Estimate  = as.numeric(tt[, "Value"]),
    SE        = as.numeric(tt[, "Std.Error"]),
    CI_low    = as.numeric(ci[params, "2.5%"]),
    CI_high   = as.numeric(ci[params, "97.5%"]),
    df        = as.numeric(tt[, "DF"]),
    t_value   = as.numeric(tt[, "t-value"]),
    p_value   = as.numeric(tt[, "p-value"]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Omit ordinary coefficient tests for the breakpoint parameters.
  omit_tests <- out$Parameter %in% blank_pvals_for
  out[omit_tests, c("df", "t_value", "p_value")] <- NA_real_

  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

# Pull every random-effect variance component present in the model.
extract_seg_ranef <- function(seg_fit, group_name) {
  vc <- as.data.frame(
    unclass(VarCorr(seg_fit$lme.fit)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  data.frame(
    Group = ifelse(rownames(vc) == "Residual", "Residual", group_name),
    Term = rownames(vc),
    Variance = as.numeric(vc$Variance),
    SD = as.numeric(vc$StdDev),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

extract_seg_fitstats <- function(seg_fit, group_name) {
  data.frame(
    Statistic = c(
      "AIC", "BIC", "logLik", "N observations",
      paste0("N groups (", group_name, ")")
    ),
    Value = c(
      AIC(seg_fit),
      BIC(seg_fit),
      as.numeric(logLik(seg_fit)),
      seg_fit$lme.fit$dims$N,
      unname(seg_fit$lme.fit$dims$ngrps[1])
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(p), "\u2013",
    ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
  )
}

# Empty row with a label in the first column, used as a section header.
make_section_header <- function(template, label) {
  header <- template[1, , drop = FALSE]
  header[] <- ""
  header[[1]] <- label
  header
}

# Build the table -----

build_seg_table <- function(m_activity_nocheat, m_activity_cheat,
                            group_name = "yearcamp", day_mean, day_sd) {

  to_days <- function(z) day_mean + z * day_sd

  tab_no  <- extract_seg_params(m_activity_nocheat)
  tab_yes <- extract_seg_params(m_activity_cheat)

  fixed_block <- full_join(
    tab_no, tab_yes,
    by = "Parameter",
    suffix = c("_No", "_Yes")
  ) %>%
    transmute(
      Row = Parameter,
      `No-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", Estimate_No, SE_No),
      `No-cheat: 95% CI` =
        sprintf("%.2f, %.2f", CI_low_No, CI_high_No),
      `No-cheat: df` =
        ifelse(is.na(df_No), "\u2013", sprintf("%.0f", df_No)),
      `No-cheat: t` =
        ifelse(is.na(t_value_No), "\u2013", sprintf("%.2f", t_value_No)),
      `No-cheat: p` =
        format_p(p_value_No),
      `Yes-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", Estimate_Yes, SE_Yes),
      `Yes-cheat: 95% CI` =
        sprintf("%.2f, %.2f", CI_low_Yes, CI_high_Yes),
      `Yes-cheat: df` =
        ifelse(is.na(df_Yes), "\u2013", sprintf("%.0f", df_Yes)),
      `Yes-cheat: t` =
        ifelse(is.na(t_value_Yes), "\u2013", sprintf("%.2f", t_value_Yes)),
      `Yes-cheat: p` =
        format_p(p_value_Yes)
    )

  # Back-transform the breakpoint and its CI from G0 to days.
  g0_no  <- tab_no  %>% filter(Parameter == "G0")
  g0_yes <- tab_yes %>% filter(Parameter == "G0")

  breakpoint_block <- data.frame(
    Row = "Breakpoint (days since incubation onset)",
    `No-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
      sprintf("%.2f", to_days(g0_no$Estimate)),
    `No-cheat: 95% CI` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f, %.2f",
        to_days(g0_no$CI_low),
        to_days(g0_no$CI_high)
      ),
    `No-cheat: df` = "\u2013",
    `No-cheat: t` = "\u2013",
    `No-cheat: p` = "\u2013",
    `Yes-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
      sprintf("%.2f", to_days(g0_yes$Estimate)),
    `Yes-cheat: 95% CI` =
      sprintf(
        "%.2f, %.2f",
        to_days(g0_yes$CI_low),
        to_days(g0_yes$CI_high)
      ),
    `Yes-cheat: df` = "\u2013",
    `Yes-cheat: t` = "\u2013",
    `Yes-cheat: p` = "\u2013",
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  ranef_no  <- extract_seg_ranef(m_activity_nocheat, group_name)
  ranef_yes <- extract_seg_ranef(m_activity_cheat, group_name)

  ranef_block <- full_join(
    ranef_no, ranef_yes,
    by = c("Group", "Term"),
    suffix = c("_No", "_Yes")
  ) %>%
    transmute(
      Row = paste0(Group, " \u2013 ", Term),
      `No-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
        sprintf("Var = %.2f, SD = %.2f", Variance_No, SD_No),
      `No-cheat: 95% CI` = "\u2013",
      `No-cheat: df` = "\u2013",
      `No-cheat: t` = "\u2013",
      `No-cheat: p` = "\u2013",
      `Yes-cheat: Estimate (SE)` =
        sprintf("Var = %.2f, SD = %.2f", Variance_Yes, SD_Yes),
      `Yes-cheat: 95% CI` = "\u2013",
      `Yes-cheat: df` = "\u2013",
      `Yes-cheat: t` = "\u2013",
      `Yes-cheat: p` = "\u2013"
    )

  list(
    fixed = fixed_block,
    breakpoint = breakpoint_block,
    random = ranef_block,
    n_fixed = nrow(fixed_block),
    n_breakpoint = nrow(breakpoint_block),
    n_random = nrow(ranef_block)
  )
}

# Stack the blocks, with a labelled header row above each.
add_section_headers <- function(tbl, blocks) {
  bind_rows(
    make_section_header(tbl$fixed, blocks[1]), tbl$fixed,
    make_section_header(tbl$fixed, blocks[2]), tbl$breakpoint,
    make_section_header(tbl$fixed, blocks[3]), tbl$random
  )
}

# Convert breakpoint to days -----
# Recover the original scaling constants from the exact linear relationship
# between ZDay and raw day, rather than rescaling the analysis subset.
day_map <- lm(
  dayordereggsleft ~ z,
  data = data.frame(
    dayordereggsleft = df_activity_allocation$dayordereggsleft,
    z = as.numeric(df_activity_allocation$ZDay)
  )
)

day_mean <- unname(coef(day_map)[1])
day_sd   <- unname(coef(day_map)[2])

# Build and display the table -----

tbl <- build_seg_table(
  m_activity_nocheat,
  m_activity_cheat,
  group_name = "Group",
  day_mean = day_mean,
  day_sd = day_sd
)

blocks <- c(
  "Fixed effects",
  "Timing of transition (days)*",
  "Random effects"
)

st_activity_display <- add_section_headers(tbl, blocks)

si_table(
  st_activity_display,
  "Extended Data Table 14. Changes in activity allocation between egg-laying and incubation over time, analysed using segmented linear mixed-effects models fitted separately for groups with and without cheats. The response variable was a logit-transformed activity allocation index, ranging from 0 (entirely egg-laying) to 1 (entirely incubation) before transformation.",
  sections = which(st_activity_display[[1]] %in% blocks),
  footnote = sprintf(
    paste(
      "*ZDay = (day \u2212 day_mean) / day_sd, where day_mean = %.2f",
      "and day_sd = %.2f days. The breakpoint back-transforms the G0",
      "estimate and 95%% CI to days since incubation onset using this",
      "relationship. df denotes denominator degrees of freedom for",
      "the coefficient t tests. Test statistics, degrees of freedom",
      "and P values are omitted for U and G0."
    ),
    day_mean, day_sd
  )
)

```

```{r Export Extended Data tables, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Write the Extended Data tables out as a spreadsheet, matching the rounding used in the document.
#A fresh workbook is built here rather than reusing Cheating_SItablesXL: that object is passed
#workbook = NULL at Extended Data Table 7, st_incubation_time and st_nest_failure, which starts a new workbook each time, so it never holds
#all of the sheets. Extended Data Table 14 is built with kable() rather than MCMCglmmProc and is added at the end.
#Extended Data Tables 5 and 13 are two-panel tables in the document, so each
#panel gets its own sheet here. Sheet names are capped at 31 characters by Excel.
si_tables <- list("Suppl. Table 1"  = st_strategy_counts,
                  "Suppl. Table 2"  = st_cheat_prop,
                  "Suppl. Table 3"  = st_cheat_prob,
                  "Suppl. Table 4"  = st_mass,
                  "Suppl. Table 5 all groups"    = st_eggs,
                  "Suppl. Table 5 excl. 1 coop"  = st_eggs_excl_1coop,
                  "Suppl. Table 6"  = st_eggs_within_female,
                  "Suppl. Table 7"  = st_laying_group,
                  "Suppl. Table 8"  = st_laying_window,
                  "Suppl. Table 9"  = st_aggression,
                  "Suppl. Table 10" = st_incubation_group,
                  "Suppl. Table 11" = st_incubation_time,
                  "Suppl. Table 12" = st_incubation_individual,
                  "Suppl. Table 13 nest failure" = st_nest_failure,
                  "Suppl. Table 13 hatching"     = st_hatch_success,
                  "Suppl. Table 14" = st_activity_display)
si_workbook  <- createWorkbook()
header_style <- createStyle(halign = "LEFT", border = "TopBottom", textDecoration = "bold")
bold_style   <- createStyle(textDecoration = "bold")
for (sheet_name in names(si_tables)) {
  tab <- si_tables[[sheet_name]]
  addWorksheet(si_workbook, sheet_name)
  writeData(si_workbook, sheet_name, tab, startCol = 1, startRow = 1, headerStyle = header_style)
  #pMCMC values below 0.05 are bolded directly, as the values are text rather than numbers
  if (ncol(tab) >= 3) {
    pvals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(tab[[3]]))
    signif_rows <- which(!is.na(pvals) & pvals < 0.05)
    if (length(signif_rows) > 0) {
      addStyle(si_workbook, sheet_name, bold_style, rows = signif_rows + 1, cols = 3,
               gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE)
    }
  }
  setColWidths(si_workbook, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol(tab), widths = "auto")
}
saveWorkbook(si_workbook,
             file = here("Scripts/Manuscripts/Frequency_dependent_cheating_SupplementaryTables.xlsx"),
             overwrite = TRUE)
```
